BLOCKER 2 (requiredKinds gate): verifyCriticalHumanProof (pipeline-state.mjs, search 'function verifyCriticalHumanProof') short-circuits on `!policy.requiredKinds.has(kind)` -- required:true then ALWAYS returns CRITICAL-PROOF-POLICY-KIND-REQUIRED (permanent brick, since project/critical-human-proof.json's requiredKinds is push/deploy/publication only and is forbidden to edit); required:false makes verification a silent no-op (defeats DoD c). Resolution (advisor-confirmed): add a small ALWAYS_REQUIRED_KINDS = new Set(['feature-package-reconcile']) bypass so the requiredKinds check is skipped for this one kind specifically, leaving push/deploy/publication behavior byte-identical. This matches ADR-0056's own 2026-08-11 Follow-up wording: 'its own always-on dependency injection point, not routed through criticalProofWaiverFor/CRITICAL_ACTION_KINDS at all today'. Add a regression test proving push is unaffected (push absent from requiredKinds + required:true must still return CRITICAL-PROOF-POLICY-KIND-REQUIRED).

That validator is consumed by plugins/pipeline-core/scripts/check-routing-projections.mjs's checkRepository(), which reads and validates the real root pipeline.user.yaml -- and that script is a REGISTERED Verify suite ('routing-projection-check', see harness/scripts/verify.mjs line ~168), not just an incidental test. runner-profiles-v3.mjs is NOT in the briefing's field-4 editable scope. Advisor's suggested resolution: implement and test the functional gates.reconcile_approval-reading logic entirely via fixture roots that parseYaml directly (exactly how critical-human-proof-policy.test.mjs's CHP16-31 already test push_approval, never touching validatePipelineUserV3), leave THIS repo's actual committed pipeline.user.yaml unedited (absent key defaults to the strongest 'signature' -- nothing is weakened by omission), and report the one-line runner-profiles-v3.mjs optional-key addition as an explicit deviation/open item requiring Elephant authorization to extend scope, rather than silently editing an out-of-scope file or silently breaking a registered Verify suite.

BINDING NOTE: verifyCriticalHumanProof requires state.activeFeature.id and state.planApproval.poGateAuthority.{planSha256,specSha256} (else CRITICAL-PROOF-STATE) -- this is the GOVERNING SESSION's own local pipeline-state.json (read via readState(dir), dir = deps.dir ?? projectDir() as computed at run()'s top, ~line 5865), NEVER the --root target repository. feature-package-reconcile is routed ahead of readState() (comment at ~5914), so the default approval wrapper must call readState(dir) itself. criticalProofWaiverFor/criticalHumanProofPolicy must also read from dir (governing session), per ADR-0056's explicit 'read from the governing session, not from the pushed repository' rule. At least one new test must fixture dir != --root to prove this isn't accidentally conflated.

NAMING NOTE: the DoD's subject binding is {manifest, planSha256, candidate} where planSha256 is the RECONCILE plan digest (--plan-sha256 flag). This is a DIFFERENT value from state.planApproval.poGateAuthority.planSha256 used internally by verifyCriticalHumanProof for feature/spec identity binding (the dev-plan digest). Do not conflate the two.

REPLAY NOTE: defaultGitCandidate's tree = 'git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}' -- the COMMITTED tree, not the working tree. A reconcile write is an uncommitted filesystem change, so candidate identity does not change across repeated invocations against the same HEAD. Reconcile also has no criticalProofConsumption-style ledger (unlike approve-push) -- nothing in the reconcile write path records a consumed proof. So a genuine replay-refusal test cannot be constructed to fail red under the one-step design; per the briefing's own explicit escape hatch (field 3, DoD bullet on replay), this must be STATED in the final report, not forced.
